title: Adaptive page orchestration and soft-fence allocator for tenant-aware spillback
author: Ava Martinez
release_notes: Introduces a tenant-aware page orchestration layer and a 'soft-fence' allocator that reduces fragmentation and smooths spillover/eviction during bursty workloads. Improves median tail latency for small requests and reduces spill I/O by delaying hard spills under short-lived pressure. Backwards-compatible; rollout via canary then gradual tenant weighting.
description:
Context: We continue to see costly hard spill events and high fragmentation on multi-tenant hosts when short-lived spikes force aggressive eviction. Existing heuristics were either too eager (triggering frequent paging) or too lazy (allowing fragmentation to grow and causing large later spills). Motivation: reduce end-to-end tail latency and I/O overhead without increasing steady-state memory usage. Goal: introduce a lightweight orchestration layer that coordinates per-tenant reservations, background reshuffle work, and a 'soft-fence' allocator that places transient allocations into a deferrable bucket so we can delay hard spill to disk for short windows of pressure.

What this PR does: Implements an Adaptive Page Orchestrator (APO) plus Soft-Fence Allocator (SFA). Key pieces: 1) Per-tenant soft-reservations that are metered and can be preemptively relaxed when higher-priority tenants need space. 2) Soft-fence bucket for transient small KV allocations; entries in the bucket are eligible for fast in-memory coalescing or lazy rewrite instead of immediate eviction to spill. 3) Background reshuffle worker that compacts fragmented pages incrementally during low-load windows. 4) Scheduling hook to prioritize reshuffle work based on observed fragmentation score and recent spill events. 5) Telemetry (new metrics) to track soft-fence occupancy, delayed-spill counts, compaction latency, and tenant preemption events.

Compatibility: Fallthroughs keep current eviction path; SFA toggles off via runtime flag to allow rollout and rollback. No schema changes.

Benchmarks: On our perf-canary cluster with mixed-size request streams (70% small, 30% large) and 12 tenants: - Median application latency improved by ~9% (from 45ms to 41ms) for small requests. - 95th percentile latency improved by ~18% for small requests. - Total spill I/O (MB/min) reduced by ~34% during 10min spike tests. - Background compaction added ~3% CPU overhead but reduced long-tail spill events significantly.

Files touched (high-level): runtime/cache/orchestrator.{h,cc}, runtime/cache/soft_fence_allocator.{cc,h}, runtime/cache/reshuffle_worker.cc, runtime/scheduler/compaction_scheduler.cc, telemetry/metrics_registry.cc, tests/cache/soft_fence_integration_test.cc, docs/ops/cache-operator-guide.md.

Rollout plan: feature gate on startup config. Canary to 10% of nodes for 48 hours, monitor new metrics and spill I/O. If stable, ramp to 50% then full rollout. If regressions observed, rollback by disabling the gate.

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc reviewed (ENG-2122)
- [x] Unit + integration tests added
- [x] Perf canary runs attached
- [x] Telemetry emitted for all key signals
- [x] Backwards-compatible flags and safe rollback

Notes: I intentionally kept reshuffle work cooperative and incremental to avoid CPU cliffs. The soft-fence bucket has an eviction age threshold to ensure we don't defer forever (default 30s). This threshold is configurable per-deployment.

review_conversation: Kenji Sato (review): Nice direction. Can you explain how preemption interacts with Dedicated tenant guarantees? We should not violate reserved capacity contracts.

Ava Martinez (author): Good point. Preemption is soft by default; for tenants with reserved capacity we bypass SFA via config. The orchestrator checks tenant_tier and honor_reservations flag before relaxing allocations.
Priya Nambiar (review): The reshuffle worker is CPU-bound in the canary. We need a circuit to back off more aggressively when host CPU > 70%.
Ava Martinez (author): Added a backoff that scales reshuffle cycles with host CPU headroom. See latest commit that samples scheduler headroom and reduces candidate window when high.
Liam O'Connor (review): Tests look good but I got flaky failure in 'soft_fence_integration_test:DeferredEvictRace'. Can you add more determinism?
Ava Martinez (author): Reworked the test to use a simulated clock and explicit yield points to remove timing-dependent flakes. Reran and green.
